subject: Proposal for GSoC 2013: RIGHT: R Interactive Graphics via HTml

messages.author: 62dac1396cf796e6
messages.subject: Proposal for GSoC 2013: RIGHT: R Interactive Graphics via HTml
parts:
Hi there -

I have posted a project proposal at the following link:

http://rwiki.sciviews.org/doku.php?id=developers:projects:gsoc2013:right

Dr. Jung Hoon Lee and I conceived this project idea (we call RIGHT)
last year from our own needs, and are willing to serve as mentors.
RIGHT aims to support easy data exploration using interactive graphics
and analysis for R and reveal information hidden among static graphs.
Although R provides awesome packages for static graphics (e.g. lattice
and ggplot2), exploring data using static graphics can be tedious;
users have to frequently interact with command line to get meaningful
graphs that answer even a simple question like “how are graphical
elements (a point or a group of points) in one graph related to those
in another graph?” Interactive graphics linking data in different
graphs and interactive visualization of summary statistics, combined
with intuitive R API for setup, can help address these questions and
make data exploration easy and also fun!

We have already hired a couple of highly-motivated students interested
in the project, one of whom we would like to team up with for GSoC. In
fact, they have been working on this project since January to make an
excellent progress so far. FYI, we post a link to a demo video which
covers a subset of the proposed functionalities implemented in HTML5
and JavaScript with an intuitive R API.

http://youtube.googleapis.com/v/thlwjYFC_yY?vq=hd1080;hd=1;autoplay=1;

Any feedback, comments, and suggestions will be highly appreciated!

Thanks,
Jae

PS It is our first time to participate in GSoC. As proposed mentors do
we need to take any action at this point?






--
Jae W. Lee, Ph.D.
Assistant Professor
Department of Semiconductor Systems Engineering
Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU)

Very impressive video. Where is the code hosted? Demo videos are
worthless without open code repositories, and GSoC is about open source
code.

> PS It is our first time to participate in GSoC. As proposed mentors do
> we need to take any action at this point?

You'll need to sign up on Google's melange system as potential mentors
for the R project after organization slots are announced next week.

You'll probably also want to communicate with one or all of the R
project admins ( e.g.,Toby, me, Virgilio, or John ) about your
qualifications and other connections with the larger R community.

Regards,

Brian
